subject: Animation
title: Jan Švankmajer: Surrealist Stop-Motion
description: A 60-second lesson on Jan Švankmajer: Surrealist Stop-Motion.

hook.text: Czech filmmaker Jan Švankmajer animated meat, bones, clay, and everyday objects into nightmarish films.

buildup.text: His work blended surrealism with stop-motion, creating deeply unsettling and strangely beautiful art.

discovery.text: Švankmajer's Alice turned Lewis Carroll's story into a genuinely disturbing puppet fever dream.

twist.text: Communist censors banned several of his films. He continued making art in secret for years.

climax.text: Švankmajer influenced Tim Burton, the Brothers Quay, and generations of experimental animators.

punchline.text: Meat and bones became art in the hands of a Czech rebel.

quiz.question: What made Jan Švankmajer's stop-motion work distinctive?
options: He used only clay for all his films
He animated unconventional materials like meat, bones, and everyday objects in surrealist narratives
